answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a stake-and-trellis reputation graph: every agent posts a small refundable bond before trading, and each completed job adds a signed endorsement linking buyer and seller, growing a trellis of work history. New identities start with tiny caps that rise only as endorsements accumulate, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs bonds plus real work each time. Like a comet, a fake burst is visible — fresh nodes with no history trading only among themselves — and a zephyr-light audit of endorsement chains exposes the cluster before it extracts value.
